title: Brijuni with Toddlers and Young Kids: Family Guide 2027
metaDescription: Brijuni with toddlers: ferry from Fažana, free entry under 7, safari park, bike trailers, dinosaur tracks, hotel options and nap-friendly planning tips.
content:
## Is Brijuni Good for Toddlers and Young Children?

Yes. Veliki Brijun, the only island with regular visitor services, has no cars. Paths are flat and mostly asphalt, and the main sights are close to the harbour. Visitors leave their cars in Fažana, on the mainland, and cross by park boat. Brijuni is not a beach resort. It is an animals-and-bikes day out, with swimming as a bonus.

## Getting There with Small Children

### Boat from Fažana
Fažana is about 10 km north of Pula. The crossing takes roughly 15 minutes. Frequency depends on season. Spring and autumn usually have 3–5 departures a day, and July–August has more. Check the park timetable the day before, because the last return boat decides how long you can stay.

### Parking and Strollers
Leave the car in Fažana and bring a lightweight stroller. Asphalt paths near the harbour handle strollers well. A stroller with large wheels is better than a compact travel stroller on gravel side paths.

## Tickets and Costs for Families

Children under 7 generally enter free. Ages 7–18 pay a reduced rate. A standard day ticket with the guided train tour runs about €35 for adults and about €17 for children aged 4–14. Expect the adult ferry and entry combination without a guided tour to cost about €30. A realistic day for one adult, with lunch and a bike, is €50–70.

If you book a taxi-boat tour from Fažana, the park entry is often not included. Entry to the small island of Sveti Jerolim is €7 for adults and €3 for children 7–18. It is free under 7. Veliki Brijun entry on those tours is about €8 for adults, and free under 7.

## What to Do on Veliki Brijun with Toddlers

### Electric Tourist Train and Safari Park
The open-sided train ride lasts about one hour and is the best first stop for toddlers. It passes the Safari Park, where zebras, llamas, ostriches and zebus live, along with Lanka, an Indian elephant given to Tito in 1970. It also passes the Roman villa remains at Verige Bay. Tours run in Croatian, Italian, German or English. After the train, the guided part continues on foot to a small church, the old quarry and the Robert Koch monument. Most toddlers will not last through this part. Leave the group after the train and head for the shade.

### Dinosaur Footprints
More than 200 dinosaur tracks are on the island, and older toddlers and preschoolers enjoy looking for them. Ask at the information point which tracks are easiest to reach with a stroller.

### Cycling with a Child Seat or Trailer
Bikes are rented at the harbour. The rental offers child seats and trailers for one or two children. A trailer is the best option for a toddler, because most nap in it within 20 minutes. The 13.3 km main trail takes about three hours, but a 6–8 km loop is enough for small children. Rental costs about €4–10 per hour. Pre-book in July and August.

### Electric Golf Cart
A cart costs about €40 per hour. It is expensive, but it is the easiest way to cover the island with a baby, and it is worth it for one hour with children under 3 in the heat of July.

### Beaches and Swimming
The swimming spots are rocky or pebbly, with limited facilities. Bring water shoes. The sea in mid-May is still cold, though children paddle anyway. Water is warmest from July to September.

## Where to Eat

Restaurants are near the harbour and the hotel. Main courses cost about €15–25 per person. Children's portions are usually available on request. Bring snacks, because options between meals are limited. There are drinking fountains on the island, so bring a refillable bottle. The shady meadows near the harbour are good for picnics and naps.

## Staying Overnight

Hotel Neptun and Hotel Karmen are on Veliki Brijun, and the park also rents out villas and houses. Hotel Neptun offers family rooms with a park view and balcony for two adults plus one child. Guests get quiet evenings when day visitors have gone, and the safari park is nearly empty in the early morning and late afternoon. Children under 12 are exempt from the €1.60 per person per night tourist tax. Ages 12–18 pay half. Luggage is moved from the pier by electric vehicle.

Overnight is the right choice for families with children under 4. A day trip means a fixed boat schedule and a missed nap, while overnight lets you ride in the morning and rest at midday.

## Best Time to Visit

- **May–June and September:** mild weather, fewer people, good for cycling.
- **July–August:** warm sea and full services, but hot, crowded and the most expensive.
- **October:** quiet. Special open days sometimes reduce guided tour tickets to about €17 for adults and €12 for ages 7–18.

Skip the panorama boat trip that circles the islands without landing if you have a toddler. It costs €15–20 per adult and you see mostly water, while the land programme is what children enjoy.

Don't pay extra for a guided on-foot tour with children under 5. The train ride is the best part, and the rest is history talk that a toddler cannot follow.

## Practical Tips for Parents

- Book the first boat of the day, to be back at the harbour before midday heat.
- Bring sun hats, sunscreen and a change of clothes. Shade is plentiful on paths but not at the dock.
- Dogs cannot go on the train, in museums or in the Safari Park.
- Bring a baby carrier as a backup for steps and gravel.
- Keep a spare ticket plan if a nap runs late: a later boat is better than a screaming return.

faq.question: Are children free on Brijuni?
faq.answer: Children under 7 generally enter Brijuni free, and ages 7–18 pay a reduced fare. A standard day ticket with the train tour is about €35 for adults and about €17 for children 4–14. Prices vary by season, so confirm before booking.

faq.question: How do you get to Brijuni with a toddler?
faq.answer: Drive to Fažana, about 10 km from Pula, and take the park boat to Veliki Brijun. The crossing takes about 15 minutes. Check the timetable for the last return boat.

faq.question: Can you take a stroller to Brijuni?
faq.answer: Yes. Paths around the harbour and main routes are flat and mostly asphalt. A stroller with larger wheels copes best, and a baby carrier is useful as a backup.

faq.question: Is it better to visit Brijuni for a day or stay overnight with young children?
faq.answer: A half day works for children over 4. For babies and toddlers, an overnight stay in Hotel Neptun or another island lodging fits naps better and avoids the day-trip crowds. Children under 12 are exempt from the tourist tax.

faq.question: What is the best activity for toddlers on Brijuni?
faq.answer: The electric train tour with the Safari Park is the best fit. It lasts about an hour and requires almost no walking. A bike with a child trailer, at around €4–10 per hour, is the second-best choice.

faq.question: Can you rent bikes with child seats on Brijuni?
faq.answer: Yes. Bikes with child seats and trailers for one or two children are available at the harbour. Book ahead in July and August.

quickAnswer: Brijuni suits toddlers and young children because Veliki Brijun is car-free, flat and compact. Boats leave from Fažana (about 15 minutes), children under 7 enter free, and the electric train and safari park cover the highlights without long walks. Plan a half day around naps, or stay overnight.
